claim_summary: CALM contributes a feedback-driven harness that performs temporal stream processing, LLM-judged anomaly curation, and continuous TimesFm fine-tuning and model swapping for adaptive time-series anomaly detection.

claim_evidence.quote: A Scalable Streaming Architecture: An end-to-end anomaly detection system architected on Apache Beam, specifically designed to handle high-throughput, out-of-order data streams.
The LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanism: A novel component that functions as an online, semantic concept drift detector.
A Closed-Loop Continuous Fine-Tuning Pipeline: A fully automated MLOps loop

modules.name: Ordered event-time window construction
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:no: the component does not embed an anomaly objective; R3_2_GTS:yes: ordered timestamps, event-time windows, watermarks and missing-time repair are its core assumptions and would need redesign for non-temporal inputs.
rubric_path: R4:Memory and Context; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: We implement a custom stateful sliding-window function to handle this. As shown in Figure 2, incoming elements are first buffered in state (per key) instead of being immediately emitted.
We include a data-cleaning step that checks each window for missing timestamps based on the expected interval.

modules.name: Quantile-forecast anomaly detector
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:yes: the component embeds the anomaly-detection output criterion by comparing forecast quantiles with the observed value; changing the task family changes the score and validation rule. R3_2_GTS is not the most specific match because the defining logic is the anomaly objective.

evidence.quote: The core anomaly detection logic uses a forecasting model (TimesFm) on each window of data. We developed a custom inference component (integrated with Beam’s “RunInference” transform) that processes each window by splitting it into a context portion and a prediction horizon.
Rather than using a single-point prediction, we leverage the model’s quantile forecasts (e.g., q20 , q30 , q70 , q80 ) to establish a robust threshold for anomalies.

modules.name: In-flight model-artifact swapping
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:no: artifact watching and weight reload do not encode a task objective. R3_2_GTS:no: the mechanism manages execution and deployment state without temporal semantics; R3_3_GH:yes.

evidence.quote: A cornerstone of the CALM framework is its ability to adapt the model on the fly. We achieve this by using Apache Beam’s side input mechanism – an auxiliary, broadcast input that can provide configuration data to all workers.
Whenever the fine-tuning stage produces a new model artifact and saves it to this location, the side input value is updated to the new model’s path.

modules.name: Semantic drift curation
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:yes: KEEP/REMOVE is a task-specific anomaly judgment that validates whether an outlier is a meaningful shift and routes the result to adaptation. R3_2_GTS is not the first match because the core criterion is the anomaly-diagnosis objective.
rubric_path: R4:Planning and Orchestration; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: Once an outlier is detected by the forecasting model, it is not immediately used for fine-tuning. Instead, it is first passed to an LLM-based classifier (the ”LLM-as-a-Judge” component) for semantic analysis.
The LLM is then tasked to decide whether to “KEEP” the anomaly (if it signifies a sustained shift in the pattern) or “REMOVE” it (if it’s a transient, one-off event).

If the decision is “KEEP,” the original data point (with its anomaly value) is forwarded to the fine-tuning pipeline. If the decision is “REMOVE,” we treat that point as a spurious outlier and replace its value with the model’s predicted value

modules.name: Continuous fine-tuning orchestration
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:no: the orchestration can reuse the same adaptation pattern for another temporal task; R3_2_GTS:yes: it requires contiguous time-series batches and temporal state to train and redeploy the model.
rubric_path: R4:Planning and Orchestration; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: The data points labeled “KEEP” by the LLM Judge are buffered and aggregated into batches for model training. We use a stateful batching mechanism that accumulates these points and only emits a batch when it has collected a full, continuous sequence
When a batch of new data is ready, the system launches a fine-tuning process for the model.
After the model is saved, the pipeline’s model-watching mechanism picks up the new model version.

temporal_validity.quote: Our experiment followed a strict temporal split to simulate a real-world scenario.

task_performance.quote: For this reason, we chose the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Area Under the Curve (AUC) score as our primary metric.

reconciliation.reason: The packet explicitly describes ordered buffering, watermark emission, and missing-timestamp checks and repair.
The side-input path watcher and callback weight reload are the same contributed mechanism.

reconciliation.reason: The source presents semantic curation and the subsequent continuous fine-tuning orchestration as distinct stages with separate reusable logic.

notes: The current card omitted the paper's custom quantile-forecast anomaly detector and did not separate the continuous fine-tuning loop from semantic curation. The LLM judge is a harness procedure because it is an in-context prompt and routing mechanism; no model parameters are updated by the judge itself.
